aspect: EXAMPLE - the call centre can read the screen and nothing else
description: An applicant stuck in background check since January 2024 asked whether phoning helps. Agents can report the status; they cannot expedite or escalate.

aspect: EXAMPLE - not even Congress can move it
description: US administrative processing is framed as a national security matter, so universities and members of Congress cannot influence speed or outcome, and once begun it cannot be stopped.
energy_note: No lever exists, at any level.

aspect: EXAMPLE - suing to get an answer, not a yes
description: The remedy is mandamus: an action to compel a decision, not a favourable one. Paying several thousand dollars to make the state do its job is standard advice, which is itself the measure of the problem.
The one intuitive self-help action - withdraw and reapply cleanly - restarts processing and triggers the same check, so the system punishes initiative.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the referral is invisible unless you pay to look
description: Referral to security screening is never announced. The only way to see it is to request GCMS notes - a separate application, with its own fee and its own wait, to discover why you are waiting.
energy_note: An application to find out about your application.

aspect: SCENARIO - the mandamus he had to fund
description: At month 31 Omid's lawyer advises a Federal Court mandamus. It costs CAD 7,500, which is most of his savings, and will compel a decision - not an approval. Six weeks after filing, the application is approved. Nobody says the two events are connected and nobody refunds the CAD 7,500.
energy_note: Paying to make the state answer, and never being told if it worked.
